rapid_method.name: Rapid first pass
rapid_method.interpretation: Domain-level initial impressions based on current knowledge. They are not indicator scores, an evidence-led HDRL assessment or a benchmark.

rapid_questions.question: How available, linkable and routinely refreshed is the data needed for research within this assessment boundary?
rapid_questions.consider: Think about coverage, refresh cycles, linkage, identifiers and whether services can work together. Do not assume that a technical possibility is routinely available.
rapid_questions.why: Research cannot be dependable when the required data are incomplete, stale, hard to link or trapped in disconnected services.

rapid_questions.question: How consistently can researchers understand, assess and reuse the data?
rapid_questions.consider: Think about terminology, metadata, quality monitoring, curated datasets and reproducible definitions—not simply whether data can be accessed.
rapid_questions.why: Available data still create delay and risk when meaning, provenance and quality are unclear.

rapid_questions.question: How clear, lawful, proportionate and predictable are governance and access arrangements?
rapid_questions.consider: Think about legal basis, access decisions, ethics, cross-border working, disclosure control, researcher accreditation and permissions.
rapid_questions.why: Trusted research needs safeguards and clear decision routes that work in practice, not governance documents alone.

rapid_questions.question: How well does the service support real research use, collaboration and reproducible delivery?
rapid_questions.consider: Think about active users, support, research outputs, multi-site delivery, training, trials and appropriate commercial access.
rapid_questions.why: Readiness should be visible in dependable research delivery and support, not infrastructure claims alone.

rapid_questions.question: How visibly are transparency, public benefit and meaningful public involvement built into the service?
rapid_questions.consider: Think about public registers, reporting, lay governance, opt-outs, engagement and independent learning or assurance.
rapid_questions.why: Trusted health-data research depends on legitimacy, understandable transparency and evidence that public benefit shapes decisions.

rapid_questions.question: How sustainable are the funding, operating model and demonstration of value?
rapid_questions.consider: Think about funding horizon, financial risk, pricing, cost recovery, partnerships and credible evidence of value.
rapid_questions.why: Capability that cannot be maintained, staffed or funded is not dependable operating capacity.

rapid_questions.question: How strong are the workforce capacity, skills, roles and service culture needed for delivery?
rapid_questions.consider: Think about staffing headroom, defined responsibilities, specialist skills, retention, workforce planning and collaboration.
rapid_questions.why: A capable platform can still fail to deliver when specialist people, operating headroom or service behaviours are missing.

rapid_questions.question: How secure, usable, resilient and scalable is the technical environment?
rapid_questions.consider: Think about secure environments, user experience, compute, storage, security operations, privacy-enhancing technology and responsible AI.
rapid_questions.why: Technical readiness requires secure and supportable operation at realistic demand, not a one-off deployment.

impression_bands.label: Starting
impression_bands.description: Capability appears limited, fragmented or mainly informal.

impression_bands.label: Developing
impression_bands.description: Plans and early capability exist, but routine delivery appears uneven.

impression_bands.label: Defined
impression_bands.description: Responsibilities and processes appear documented and in regular use.

impression_bands.label: Managed
impression_bands.description: Performance appears measured, standardised and actively managed.

impression_bands.label: Continuously improving
impression_bands.description: Learning, comparison and improvement appear systematic and sustained.

A.common_mistake: Counting data that exist somewhere as research-ready without checking coverage, refresh, linkage permissions and routine delivery.
dependencies: C: lawful access and linkage governance
H: secure infrastructure and data flows

B.common_mistake: Treating a one-off mapping or data dictionary as evidence of consistently governed semantics and quality.
dependencies: A: representative and current source data

C.common_mistake: Equating a written policy with an operating pathway that is understood, measured and used consistently.

D.common_mistake: Counting projects or publications without defining the denominator, period, service contribution or quality of support.
dependencies: A–C: usable data and workable governance
G: service and research support capacity

E.common_mistake: Treating one-way communications as meaningful involvement, or publication alone as evidence that transparency is useful.
dependencies: D: evidence of research use and benefit

F.common_mistake: Treating current funding as sustainability without testing renewal risk, cost recovery, demand and operating liabilities.

G.common_mistake: Counting posts rather than funded capacity, specialist competence, retention risk and headroom for real demand.
dependencies: D: user support and service demand

H.common_mistake: Treating certification, procurement or a successful pilot as evidence of secure, usable and scalable operation.

recommendation_rules.when: A maturity judgement has no linked evidence record.
recommendation_rules.output: Treat the judgement as provisional and ask what document, metric, audit record or other source could substantiate it.

recommendation_rules.when: A response is marked high uncertainty or not known.
recommendation_rules.output: Identify the person closest to this capability and the evidence needed to resolve the uncertainty.

recommendation_rules.when: An indicator has not been assessed.
recommendation_rules.output: Decide whether the indicator is relevant, who should review it and by when.

recommendation_rules.when: The assessor records an improvement note.
recommendation_rules.output: Carry the assessor's own proposed action into the report with a link back to the indicator; do not invent an action.

recommendation_rules.when: Independent team judgements span more than one adjacent maturity level or use different applicability statuses.
recommendation_rules.output: Review interpretation, scope and evidence before agreeing a consensus; do not average the responses.
